Apple has reported a record $117.3 billion in research and development spending in its quarterly results, continuing a sharply accelerating trend of expenditures throughout fiscal year 2026. Details below.

Apple Increases R&D Spending

Last quarter, Apple reported $11.4 billion in R&D spending, a 34% year-over-year increase.

During the company's earnings call, Cook said Apple is "clearly investing more," adding that R&D spending is "growing much faster than the company as a whole."

He subsequently reiterated that R&D spending is "indeed expanding significantly on a year-over-year basis," particularly when discussing Apple's AI investments. Apple's CFO Kevan Parekh added that AI spending is being layered on top of Apple's regular product roadmap investments.

Today, Apple reported a record $117.3 billion in R&D spending for the third quarter of 2026, a 32% year-over-year increase, bringing Apple's total R&D spending so far in fiscal year 2026 to $340.4 billion.

For comparison, Apple's R&D spending for the entirety of fiscal year 2025 was $345.5 billion. This means the company has nearly matched last year's full-year total with one quarter remaining, while already surpassing the full-year R&D spending of fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Over the past few days, Wall Street has punished companies that announce accelerated AI-related spending without demonstrating equally clear short-term returns.

Alphabet's shares fell 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion, to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion. Meta's shares also fell by roughly 9% to 10%, as it raised the lower end of its full-year capital expenditure forecast to $130 billion while free cash flow plummeted 91%.

Apple's shares are currently down roughly 4% in after-hours trading. This reaction may shift again during the earnings call and again during regular trading hours tomorrow.
